title: Code Owns the Simulation, Jev Owns the Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2610.01834v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Judgment models such as \jev{} return, in a single call and without reasoning text, a probability for each described option. This makes them attractive as an agent's action-selection layer, but it is unclear which decisions they can be trusted with. We test \jev{} on reflection tests, one-shot matrix games, the text game ALFWorld and robot control, and find a sharp boundary. \jev{} succeeds when the right option can be judged from what the input describes, which we call \emph{evaluation}. Specifically, it solves 99\% of the counterintuitive Cognitive Reflection Test questions. However, it fails when the right option depends on \emph{simulation} (i.e., predicting something not in the input), such as the opponent's action or the subgoal that must come first. In games, \jev{} plays suboptimally as if its rational opponent acted at random, because the opponent's action is not given. In ALFWorld, \jev{} favors commands that mention an object

translated_title: 代码负责模拟，Jev负责评估
translated_abstract: 判断模型（如Jev）能够在单次调用中、无需生成推理文本的情况下，直接返回每个被描述选项的概率。这使得它们作为智能体的动作选择层颇具吸引力，但目前尚不清楚它们可以胜任哪些决策。我们在反思测试、一次性矩阵博弈、文本游戏ALFWorld和机器人控制任务上测试了Jev，并发现了一个清晰的分界线。当正确选项可以从输入所描述的内容中直接判断出来时，Jev能够成功，我们将此称为“评估”。具体来说，它解决了99%的反直觉认知反思测试（Cognitive Reflection Test）题目。然而，当正确选项依赖于“模拟”（即预测输入中不存在的信息）时，例如对手的行动或必须优先完成的子目标，Jev就会失败。在博弈中，Jev的表现是次优的，表现得仿佛其理性对手是在随机行动，因为对手的行动并未在输入中给出。在ALFWorld中，Jev倾向于选择提及某个对象的命令（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文发现判断模型Jev在“评估”任务（正确选项可直接从输入描述中判断，如解决99%的认知反思测试题）上表现出色，但在需要“模拟”的任务（需预测输入中不存在的信息，如对手行动或前置子目标）上会系统性地失败。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals a sharp boundary in judgment models like Jev: they excel at "evaluation" (judging options directly describable from the input, solving 99% of Cognitive Reflection Test questions) but fail at "simulation" (predicting information absent from the input, such as an opponent's action or prerequisite subgoals).
